correctness.rationale: Mostovoy Theorem 1 gives rational homology concentrated in two 1D degrees nd,(n-1)d for even d and one degree t=ceil(n/2)(d+1)-1 for odd d>=3. Every reflection-fixed unordered finite subset decomposes uniquely into j equatorial points and k antipodal off-equator pairs j+2k<=n; compactly supported configuration Euler generating series is (1+z)^{χ(S^{d-1})}(1+z²)^{χ_c(R^d)}, equal to 1+z² for even d or (1+z)²/(1+z²) for odd d. Summing coefficients 1..n gives fixed χ=1 (even), 2 (odd n=1,2 mod4), 0 (odd n=0,3 mod4). Lefschetz and connectedness recover odd-dimensional reflection sign (-1)^ceil(n/2). In even d, orientation on dense n-distinct-point manifold gives top sign (-1)^n; Lefschetz fixes lower sign (-1)^(n-1). Since SO(d+1) is connected this determines full determinant characters; rational G-invariant cellular cochains compute homology of any finite orthogonal quotient. Independent coefficient/quotient checks held for 9672 parameter pairs; exact proof covers all n,d.

value.rationale: Natural O(d+1) symmetry is intrinsic to finite subsets of the standard sphere, and finite orthogonal orbit spaces are canonical derived topological objects. Rank-only results cannot answer whether a reflection kills a homology generator. The theorem provides a complete graded rational character classification and an exact modulo-four dichotomy for infinitely many odd-dimensional orientation-reversing quotients; this is a motivated natural all-parameter structural invariant, not an arbitrary special value.
